channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Third supertanker hit by mine in Hormuz, IRGC says rules violations will be met with force
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: IRGC Navy confirms third supertanker hit by sea mine in Hormuz strait since Saturday; U.S. escort ships withdrawn. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: U.S. accepted some of Iran's seven conditions; Rezaei says response is insufficient
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: U.S. accepted some of Iran's seven conditions conveyed through Qatar in September; National Security Council Secretary Rezaei found the response insufficient. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Some countries filed suit over Minab school attack; Iran pressing legal case
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Deputy Legal Advisor of Foreign Ministry Garibabadi said some foreign countries have filed suits over the Minab school attack; legal process continues. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Petropars workers in Khuzestan flogged for protesting layoffs; worker councils call for widespread demonstrations
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: More than 10 Petropars workers in Khuzestan who resisted layoffs have been flogged; two worker councils called for large-scale protest. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Zarif says Iran lacks enriched uranium for nuclear bomb
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Former Foreign Minister Zarif argues nuclear weapons aren't deterrents, claiming Iran lacks the enriched uranium needed to make an atomic bomb. (Source: Khabaronline)

item.title: Missile attack on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport: 12 dead, conflicting figures
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Ansarallah's missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed at least 12 people; casualty figures vary among sources. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: What happened to a tanker in Hormuz? Revolutionary Guards say "mine," CENTCOM says "air strike"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A burning tanker near Hormuz: Revolutionary Guards claim mine strike, CENTCOM claims air strike, UKMTO calls it accident. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: Trump says he is in contact with Ansarallah following Riyadh strike
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Trump said the U.S. is in contact with Ansarallah following the Riyadh airport strike; left unclear whether the U.S. will directly enter the conflict. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Turkey publishes regulations implementing social media ban for under-15s
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkey's Official Gazette published regulations enforcing the social media restriction for children under 15; the law takes effect November 1. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: 11 million people receive 500,000-toman increase in food allowance; other households in limbo
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Iran disbursed 500,000 tomans in food allowance to 11 million under Emdad and Welfare; timeline for others unclear. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: U.S. calls on Turkey and Pakistan: Close overland routes to Iran
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent said he has discussed with Turkey and Pakistan closing overland access to Iran; "absolute isolation" campaign expands. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Kalibaf to Rubio: You'll face Valerian's fate, you'll kneel
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Kalibaf, Zarif, and government spokesman Mohajerani replied to Rubio's Athens comments on Iran with historical allusions; polemic continues. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia: Fire at Abqaiq, hundreds of flights halted in Riyadh
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Yemeni Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi facilities in Riyadh and Yanbu; fire broke out at Abqaiq refinery, hundreds of flights were canceled. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Pentagon quietly updates Iran war casualty figures: numbers rise
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Per ISNA, Pentagon silently updated official casualty figures in Iran war; actual toll appears higher per Washington Post sources. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: World Day Against Death Penalty: 2,003 executed in Iran in one year
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Report released on World Day Against Death Penalty shows 2,003 people executed in Iran in the past year; at least 69 for political-security charges. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Trump: US will not attack Iran before November 3 midterm elections
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Trump posted on Truth Social that the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections; Israeli alert level was raised the same day. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Putin to Pezeshkian: Convey my respect to the esteemed Supreme Leader
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Putin met Pezeshkian at the CIS summit in Turkmenistan; Russia said it would provide diplomatic support to resolve the Middle East crisis. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: US adds 27 companies and 22 ships linked to Iran's shadow fleet to sanctions list
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The U.S. Treasury added 6 individuals, 27 companies, and 22 vessels linked to Iran's shadow fleet to sanctions. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: European Parliament passes resolution on Iran: calls for abolishing capital punishment and broader sanctions
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The European Parliament passed a resolution with 541 votes calling for abolishing capital punishment in Iran and broader sanctions. (Source: Khabaronline)

item.title: China turns to Iraqi oil: Is Iran circumventing the embargo the old way?
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Chinese independent refineries are shifting to Iraqi crude to compensate for declining Iranian oil; experts say origin labels may not reflect true sources. (Source: Iran International)
